chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
“Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment regarding an owned slave who attributed a man to other than his father. He said: ‘I hold that his skin should be stripped bare.’”

He said: “And he said regarding a man who had been attributed to other than his father: ‘Establish your proof, and I will enable you against him.’ Then when he produced the proof, he said: ‘Indeed his mother was a slave woman.’ He said: ‘There is no hadd upon you. Insult him as he insulted you, and pardon him if you wish.’”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: “This report is weak, contrary to what we have previously presented of sound reports and to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, so it should not be acted upon. Moreover, within it is that which weakens it further, namely that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ordered the litigant to insult his opponent as he had insulted him, and it is not جائز from him عليه السلام that he should command that. Rather, what pertains to him is to take for him his right from his opponent by establishing the hadd against him, if he is among those upon whom that is obligatory, or to discipline him if he is not. As for commanding him to exchange insults, that is something not permissible in any circumstance.”

key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an as a source of legal and doctrinal authority
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: weak in transmission or evidentiary standing
key_terms.قَضَى: gave judgment or issued a legal ruling
key_terms.لِغَيْرِ أَبِيهِ: to other than his father; false attribution of lineage
key_terms.يُعَزِّرَهُ: to discipline him with discretionary punishment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about falsely attributing someone to other than his father, and why was it judged weak?
ai.summary: This report relates legal judgments concerning falsely attributing a person to other than his father and includes a later scholarly note declaring the narration weak. The closing statement rejects acting upon it because it conflicts with sound reports and the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, especially regarding the idea of commanding reciprocal insult.
